#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup
/area testing

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Shards the `sequential/extended` e2e suite so the heavy Spark setup is isolated, following the same feature-label sharding approach as the `singlecluster/extended` suite (#11964). The suite is split into two shards:
  
- shard-0 (`feature:managejobswithoutqueuename`, `feature:workloadidentifierannotations`): 9 specs; installs jobset/lws/appwrapper.
- shard-1 (`feature:spark`): 2 specs; installs only the Spark operator + image.
  
Current pre-shard runtimes (`hack/tools/prow-runtimes`, last 6 successful runs):

| Job | Avg |
|---|---:|
| `periodic-kueue-test-e2e-sequential-extended-main` | 18:27 |
| `pull-kueue-test-e2e-sequential-extended-main` | 21:12 |

## Walkthrough

Test sharding infrastructure is added to the e2e-sequential-extended suite. Two new make targets invoke the parent target with shard-specific label filters. Two test suites are labeled to enable splitting by feature.

## Changes

**E2E Sequential Extended Test Sharding**

| Layer / File(s) | Summary |
|---|---|
| **Test feature labels** <br> `test/e2e/sequential/extended/managejobswithoutqueuename_test.go` | Two test suites are labeled with `feature:managejobswithoutqueuename` to enable test filtering by the sharding infrastructure. |
| **Makefile sharding targets** <br> `Makefile-test.mk` | Two new `.PHONY` make targets `test-e2e-sequential-extended-shard-0` and `test-e2e-sequential-extended-shard-1` are added. Each target sets `GINKGO_ARGS` with shard-specific label filters and delegates execution to the parent `test-e2e-sequential-extended` target. |

## Possibly related issues

- kubernetes-sigs/kueue#11988: Implements the requested CI sharding optimization by adding shard-specific make targets and feature labels to filter the e2e-extended suite into discrete shards.
- kubernetes-sigs/kueue#11990: Adds make targets to split the periodic e2e-sequential-extended job into sharded runs by feature labels, implementing the requested CI job sharding.
